title: Find a Real Problem
outcome: By the end, I can turn a recorded problem into a bounded, measurable project goal.
scenario: A fictional class loses time finding the correct craft tray.
given: In eight recorded requests, three selected trays lack a required tool; five match.
The teacher permits a paper finder using fictional requests and an approved tray list, with no pupil names.

steps.label: Observe problem
steps.detail: Three mismatches are recorded out of eight requests.

steps.label: Define need
steps.detail: Help users choose a tray containing every requested tool.

steps.label: Set success test
steps.detail: Compare selected tray against the approved inventory for each new case.

steps.label: Bound the project
steps.detail: Use fictional tool requests; do not collect identity or purchase equipment.

explanation: The mismatch record describes a concrete need. A measurable goal checks whether the chosen tray satisfies the request; calling the system smart would not tell us how to evaluate it. Start with a transparent paper baseline, and keep unsatisfied requests visible instead of selecting a near match without warning.

counterfactual.change: The approved list contains no tray with every requested tool.
counterfactual.prediction: The finder should report no suitable tray rather than guess.
counterfactual.reason: Success includes honestly identifying unsatisfied requirements.

student_task: Write a one-sentence project goal and say what evidence would count as a failure.
teacher_answer: Goal: choose an inventory-confirmed tray containing all requested tools or report none. A selected tray missing a required tool is a failure.
project_evidence: For the Helpful Classroom Sorter, retain the problem record, permitted scope, baseline and observable acceptance criteria.
limits: Eight requests do not show the problem’s frequency across the entire school or prove AI is necessary.
review_note: Individually reviewed fictional topic example; arithmetic and declared policies checked. This is supported practice, not the reserved independent assessment.
